clue.text: Angry artists in Indian city now recalled

blocks.note: mad is an informal word for angry
RA is a Royal Academician, so artists are RAS

explanation.surface: Furious painters are summoned back from a city in India.
explanation.walkthrough: MADRAS was renamed Chennai in 1996, so it is a city that has since been called by another name: 'recalled' means re-called, not summoned home.
explanation.definitionFit: Madras is the former name of Chennai, the port city in southern India that was officially renamed.

clue.text: Putting queen on ten is appropriate

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting one thing on another stacks it above, so the first piece comes before the second

blocks.note: Queen Anne, who reigned over Britain from 1702 to 1714
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A card player decides that laying a queen on a ten is the proper move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as the adjective 'suitable' but is the verb, to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To annex territory is to seize it and take possession, which is what appropriating means as a verb.

clue.text: Lose voter, unfortunately, as president

indicators.note: something that has turned out unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A candidate's bad luck in losing a supporter on the way to the presidency.
explanation.definitionFit: Two Roosevelts, Theodore and Franklin D., served as President of the United States.

clue.text: Bones in front and back area

blocks.note: the stern is the back end of a ship
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: An anatomy lesson on the bones at the front and back of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front and back' reads as a pair of opposites, but 'front' belongs to the definition and 'back' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone at the front of the chest, and its Latin plural gives the word here.

clue.text: Being a part-timer, getting extra time is attractive

indicators.note: getting something extra means taking in an addition, so one piece is slipped inside the other

blocks.note: working as a temp, a temporary office worker
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A part-time worker finds that being offered overtime makes the job appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting extra time' reads as working overtime; it means one more letter slipped inside the part-timer's activity. A temp is a temporary office worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tempting draws you towards it, which is a close synonym for attractive or enticing.

clue.text: Which people kiss and tell, without restraint?

definitions.text: Which people kiss and tell, without restraint?

blocks.clueFragment: Which people kiss and tell, without restraint?
blocks.note: surface reading: something gossips do, kissing someone and then telling everyone about it
setter's reading: an Irish landmark that visitors kiss, after which they are said to talk freely and fluently

explanation.walkthrough: Legend says kissing the stone at Blarney Castle, near Cork in Ireland, gives the gift of the gab; 'kiss and tell' is split into kissing it and then talking without restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Blarney means smooth flattering talk, the eloquence the castle's famous stone is said to grant whoever kisses it.

clue.text: Buddhist symbol unknown in Asian city

blocks.note: a mandala is a circular symbolic diagram used in Buddhist meditation
algebra uses x, y and z for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: A Buddhist emblem is found somewhere in an Asian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but only links the wordplay to the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandalay is the second city of Myanmar (Burma), its former royal capital.

clue.text: Put into the bargain about a thousand yen as capital

indicators.note: the outer piece is placed around the letters that follow the word about
about means surrounding, so the outer piece wraps round the inner letters

blocks.note: into the bargain means as well, in addition
K is short for kilo, a thousand
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: A trader throws in about a thousand yen extra to sweeten a deal for capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money alongside the yen; it is a capital city, and the yen hints at which.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokyo is the capital city of Japan, whose currency is the yen.

clue.text: In dark, possibly lone source of illumination

indicators.note: possibly says the word is one of several arrangements its letters could take
in places the rearranged letters inside the word for dark

blocks.note: night as a noun, the dark
taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: In the dark, perhaps a single light is all there is to see by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dark' is a noun here, the night; the rearranged letters go in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A neon light is a glowing gas-filled tube, a lamp that gives illumination.

clue.text: Stupidly refuse one proposition, ultimately? That’s surprising

indicators.note: done stupidly means done badly and out of order, so the letters get muddled
ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the last letter of proposition

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly turns down a final offer, and the onlooker is astonished.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the exclamation 'That's surprising', read as a description: something unforeseen is surprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Unforeseen means not predicted or expected, so whatever it describes comes as a surprise.

clue.text: As we say, not a complex problem

indicators.note: as we say points to the spoken word, so what counts is how it is pronounced

blocks.note: the K is silent, so the two words are pronounced the same

explanation.surface: Someone explains, in their own phrase, that a matter is simple after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a complex problem' reads as one phrase meaning easy; split it after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot is a tangle that is hard to undo, so figuratively an intricate difficulty or puzzle.

clue.text: Never finishing without vote involving other nations

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: never ending, everlasting
a cross is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Endless diplomacy without any vote on matters between countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking but here means outside, its old sense; the cross goes in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: External affairs are a country's foreign relations, its dealings with other states abroad.

clue.text: Deity as source of name for far-flung missions

definitions.text: source of name for far-flung missions

blocks.note: first meaning: the Greek and Roman god of the sun, music and prophecy

blocks.clueFragment: source of name for far-flung missions
blocks.note: second meaning: the NASA lunar programme of 1961 to 1972, named after that god

explanation.surface: A god lends his name to missions sent to distant lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missions' suggests missionaries spreading a faith, but these are space missions to the Moon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek and Roman sun god lent his name to the NASA programme that landed astronauts on the Moon.

clue.text: Entertain lavishly, and a lot, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means what follows is judged by its sound when spoken

blocks.note: one's lot is one's destiny, and the two words are pronounced alike

explanation.surface: A host throws a lavish party and spends a great deal on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' looks like 'plenty', but means one's lot in life.
explanation.definitionFit: To fete someone is to honour them with celebrations, treating them as a guest of honour.

clue.text: Work of master auctioned off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters are not in their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Old Master painting goes under the hammer at a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'master' suggests a great painter, but here it is a schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster's job is teaching, so the instruction given to pupils is his work.

clue.text: Source of information or instruction, by the way

definitions.text: Source of information or instruction, by the way

blocks.clueFragment: Source of information or instruction, by the way
blocks.note: surface reading: an aside about a manual or teacher, with by the way meaning incidentally
setter's reading: literally beside the road, where a posted notice tells drivers where to go or what to do

explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' is usually a throwaway phrase; read literally it means at the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice posted beside a road gives directions, distances, warnings or instructions to motorists.

clue.text: Times arranged clues she’d composed

indicators.note: composed means put together or made up, so the letters are assembled afresh

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A crossword setter for The Times has arranged the clues she wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a Times setter; 'Times' is really ordinary times, and 'arranged' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Schedules are timetables, lists of planned times at which events or tasks are fixed to happen.

clue.text: Noble officer that opens up at the front

definitions.text: that opens up at the front

blocks.note: first meaning: the 7th Earl of this title, who led the Charge of the Light Brigade in the Crimean War

blocks.clueFragment: that opens up at the front
blocks.note: second meaning: a knitted woollen jacket that buttons down the front

explanation.walkthrough: 'opens up at the front' sounds like an officer starting an attack, which fits the earl's charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The knitted jacket is named after the Crimean War earl, who is said to have worn one.

clue.text: A couple of legal actions that traveller may take

blocks.note: a suit is a lawsuit
a case is a matter brought before a court

explanation.surface: A traveller may find themselves facing a pair of lawsuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A couple of legal actions' asks for two different words for a lawsuit, joined together.
explanation.definitionFit: Travellers carry their clothes and belongings in luggage, a case with a handle.

clue.text: Detest hearties, oddly enough

indicators.note: oddly means keeping the letters in odd positions, first, third, fifth and so on

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Someone, strangely, cannot stand jolly, back-slapping types.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly enough' reads as 'strangely'; here it means the odd-numbered letters. Hearties are boisterous, outdoorsy people.
explanation.definitionFit: To hate is to loathe or feel strong dislike, the same verb as detest.

clue.text: Where rook is immobilised, initially, in trap

blocks.note: first meaning: the square of the chessboard where a rook stands, hemmed in, at the start of a game
second meaning: to drive into a position with no escape

explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal; it means at the start of the game, when each rook sits boxed in at the board's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To corner someone is to trap them, leaving them nowhere to go; the rook starts the game in a corner square.

clue.text: Turned and fled police force

blocks.note: ran away, fled
the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A suspect wheeled round and ran from the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' suggests turning on one's heel, but it means gone sour, as milk turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has turned has gone off, stale and sour-smelling, which is what rancid describes.

clue.text: Graph showing daily temperature

blocks.note: a daily is a cleaning lady who comes in each day, also called a char or charwoman
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A hospital graph recording a patient's temperature each day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' is a British noun for a cleaner, not an adjective about days.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart is a diagram plotting figures, the same thing as a graph.

clue.text: Information on second reduction in rate

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the second piece follows the first

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
the lowdown is the inside information on something

explanation.surface: Data on a second cut in the interest rate.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests finance, a cut in interest rates; the definition is a drop in speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A slowdown is a decrease in speed or pace of activity, so a fall in the rate.

clue.text: Old way monarch becomes more like Charles V

blocks.note: wise is an archaic noun for way or manner, as in 'in no wise'
R is short for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned king turns into someone resembling the Holy Roman Emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles V of France was called Charles the Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles V of France was nicknamed le Sage, so anyone more like him has greater sagacity.

clue.text: City, second in flight, as announced by pilot

indicators.note: second in picks out the letter in the second position of the next word
pilots spell letters over the radio with code words, so the letter is swapped for its radio name

blocks.note: the second letter of flight

explanation.surface: A pilot announces the city where a flight lands.
explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO phonetic alphabet used in radio, each letter has a code word, and L is called LIMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru.

clue.text: Without any reason, reduced production of flour, say

blocks.note: grain is ground to make flour, so flour is a ground product
reduced, smaller in amount

explanation.surface: For no reason, a mill cut its output of flour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks flour as one example of something ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundless means having no basis or foundation, so an accusation made without justification.

clue.text: Ancients translated, for example

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so the letters are rendered in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Translating classical writers, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'for instance' means for example, so the noun stands in for example.

clue.text: Platforms set back in ramparts, originally

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across them
set back means moved backwards, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Viewing platforms were first built set back within the castle walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' looks like a first-letter signal but is only part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Rostra are raised platforms for speakers, the plural of rostrum.
